text:
laura: Heads-up — starting onboarding for Newt-7B. License has some weird clauses around redistribution and attribution. Planning to run quant evals this week. Can legal/ops advise?

josh: paste the exact clause pls

laura: ```
Section 4. Redistribution and Derivatives: Redistribution of model weights (including quantized or converted binaries) is prohibited without explicit written permission. Hosting model as a service for non-commercial research is permitted with attribution. Commercial use prohibited unless licensed.
```

josh: hmm. two quick asks: (1) does "hosting as a service" include offering an API? (2) does quantized weights count as "redistribution"? 

priya: what's our intended deployment: hosted API sandbox for evals then dedicated for customers? or private only?

laura: start with internal evals on dedicated, then hosted eval endpoints for partners. We'll be producing qweights (q4/q8) in the repo for benchmarks.

nate: so if we're generating qweights for benchmarks, are we allowed to store them in our artifact repo? or would that be considered redistribution?

josh: legal POV: two parts — offering inference (API) is typically allowed under "hosting as a service" language, so that's ok for evaluation/demo. However storing or publishing weight files (including quantized binaries) in an internal artifact repo that could be downloaded by users/build systems may be treated as redistribution. If the clause prohibits redistribution of "converted binaries" explicitly, we can't keep downloadable qweights in shared buckets.

josh: also: attribution required. Need to surface required text on any UI/docs where model results are shown.

emily: compliance note: update onboarding checklist: - no public artifact downloads - lock qweights in gated storage - KMS keys + access audit - add required attribution string in model metadata and UI

laura: quick question: are embeddings or downstream derivatives impacted? e.g., storing vector DB chunks from inference

josh: embeddings are model outputs, not weights — licensing typically allows output use unless license says otherwise. Still document it for customers.

priya: deploy-bot will scan build artifacts. if a commit includes a binary with "newt" and signature patterns we'll block. tagging infra owners: @priya

deploy-bot: artifact-scan: flagged binary 'newt_q4.bin' in /artifacts/jenkins/ for potential redistribution clause. Action: blocked from release.

nate: workaround: keep quantized weights only on dedicated/private clusters, never check into generic artifact repos. For hosted evals use ephemeral volume mounts and do in-cluster quantization, then delete.

josh: suggest we reach out to upstream licensor for a commercial license if we want to ship hosted commercial product. Legal can draft a request. @laura please open a ticket.

laura: I'll open a legal request + add checklist items. Priya will set artifact gating, Nate will update eval repo to avoid checked-in qweights. 

emily: sounds good :thumbsup:

laura: tagging owners: laura, josh, priya, nate, emily. I'll follow up with PR for onboarding doc changes.
